data.title: Circuit Breaker
data.tagline: A circuit breaker cuts off a repeatedly failing dependency, fails fast or degrades, and probes recovery later
data.learningOutcome: You can use Closed, Open, and Half-Open to explain breaker behavior and distinguish it from timeout and retry.
data.description: When a checkout page calls a payment dependency that keeps timing out, continuing to wait and retry can exhaust the caller's threads and request queue. A breaker moves through Closed, Open, and Half-Open: normal calls pass while Closed; repeated failures open it for fast failure or fallback; a later limited probe tests recovery, returning to Closed on success or Open on failure. It is different from one timeout or retry and cannot repair the dependency.

learning.assumes: You have seen dependency timeouts, failed requests, or degraded service.
learning.outcome: You can use Closed, Open, and Half-Open to explain breaker behavior and distinguish it from timeout and retry.

explanation.title: Problem and key mechanism
explanation.text: Repeated dependency timeouts or failures accumulate waiting and resource use at the caller; after crossing the threshold, the circuit breaker moves from Closed to Open for fast failure or fallback, then allows only a small probe in Half-Open after a pause.

explanation.title: Feedback decides recovery
explanation.text: A successful probe returns to Closed; a failed probe opens the circuit again. The caller is protected, but the breaker does not repair or guarantee the dependency.

explanation.title: A second scenario: weather lookup
explanation.text: A trip page depends on an external weather API. After repeated failures, it can temporarily return a cached forecast with its update time and stop calling the dependency, then use a few probes before restoring normal lookup.

data.boundary: A timeout sets how long one call waits, and a retry sets how many more attempts happen. A breaker decides whether repeated failure should temporarily stop calls. It usually works with bounded retries and an explicit fallback.

lessonPractice.title: The payment dependency keeps failing while new checkout requests wait. What should the circuit breaker do next?

options.label: Enter Open, fail fast or degrade, then probe later in Half-Open
options.feedback: Correct. Open isolates the failure; Half-Open uses limited probes to learn whether the dependency recovered.

options.label: Keep increasing retries so every request waits for payment success
options.feedback: Unlimited retries consume caller resources; the breaker exists to stop the failure spreading.

options.label: Return to Closed immediately and send every new request to the failing dependency
options.feedback: Closing immediately would amplify the failure again; probe recovery before returning to normal calls.

data.agentPrompt: Add a circuit breaker around the payment dependency: stay Closed normally, enter Open after repeated failures with fast failure or a clear fallback, then move to Half-Open for a small recovery probe. Return to Closed only after success. Simulate timeouts and recovery, and verify the state, user feedback, and probe are observable.
